entries.name: AI Software
entries.rationale: A compromised AI library cannot be recognised from evidence alone; what is observable is install-time behaviour such as lifecycle scripts that reach into the agent.

entries.name: Data

entries.name: Model

entries.name: Container Registry
entries.rationale: A manipulated image under a trusted tag looks identical to the real one from the host; AgentDFIR does not verify registry contents.

entries.name: AI Agent Tool
entries.rationale: Agent tools, MCP packages, plugins and skills are on disk and in configuration, and their provenance and drift are what the supply-chain rules check.

entries.name: User Execution

entries.name: Unsafe AI Artifacts

entries.name: Malicious Package
entries.rationale: Package installs from URLs, downloaded files executed, and install scripts touching the agent are all in command and process evidence.

entries.name: Poisoned AI Agent Tool
entries.rationale: Invoking a poisoned tool leaves its definition in the MCP configuration and its response in the transcript or gateway log, both of which are inspected for instruction content.

entries.name: Malicious Link
entries.rationale: The click itself is at most a browser-history entry; what AgentDFIR sees is a download followed by execution.

entries.name: Valid Accounts
entries.rationale: Use of a valid account is legitimate by construction; identity switches inside related activity and explicit-credential logons are the observable signals.

entries.name: External Harms
entries.rationale: External harms are outcomes in the world, not evidence on a host; the actions that cause them are mapped to their own techniques.

entries.name: Financial Harm
entries.rationale: Financial harm is an outcome, not host evidence.

entries.name: Reputational Harm
entries.rationale: Reputational harm is an outcome, not host evidence.

entries.rationale: Societal harm is an outcome, not host evidence.

entries.name: User Harm

entries.name: AI Intellectual Property Theft
entries.rationale: The theft is an exfiltration; the transfer is observable, but nothing tells a model or dataset apart from other files that leave.

entries.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
entries.rationale: Exploitation of an internet-facing service is evidenced in that service's logs, which AgentDFIR does not collect.

entries.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
entries.rationale: Shell and interpreter execution by the agent is recorded in transcripts and process telemetry.

entries.name: LLM Prompt Injection
entries.rationale: Injected instructions sit in content the agent read (instruction files, tool results, prompts) and are matched for override phrasing.

entries.name: Direct
entries.rationale: A direct injection is the user turn itself, recorded verbatim in the transcript.

entries.name: Indirect
entries.rationale: Indirect injections arrive in repository files, tool results and fetched content, all of which the transcript or gateway log records.

entries.name: Triggered
entries.rationale: The triggering event is often outside the examined systems; standing instructions that fire on every run are observable in memory files.

entries.name: Phishing
entries.rationale: Phishing is delivered by mail or messaging systems AgentDFIR does not examine.

entries.name: Spearphishing via Social Engineering LLM
entries.rationale: Social engineering through an LLM targets people outside the examined hosts.

entries.name: Deepfake-Assisted Phishing
entries.rationale: Deepfake phishing targets people through channels AgentDFIR does not examine.

entries.name: AI Agent Tool Invocation
entries.rationale: Every tool call is in the transcript and, when present, the MCP gateway log, together with the auto-approval settings that let it run.

entries.name: LLM Jailbreak
entries.rationale: Jailbreak prompts are in the transcript; known templates are matched, novel ones are not.

entries.name: Unsecured Credentials
entries.rationale: Reads of credential files, keys, cloud credentials and honeytokens are in commands, file events and process telemetry.

entries.name: Extract LLM System Prompt
entries.rationale: System-prompt extraction attempts are prompts recorded in the transcript.

entries.name: LLM Data Leakage
entries.rationale: Credential material in the conversation, in URLs or echoed from the environment is in the transcript.

entries.name: Erode Dataset Integrity
entries.rationale: Targets model training or inference internals (weights, datasets, inference APIs) that an endpoint and agent forensic tool does not collect.

entries.name: Publish Hallucinated Entities
entries.rationale: Registering the hallucinated name is adversary-side; on the host only the install of an unfamiliar package is visible, and no rule can tell a hallucinated name from a real one.

entries.name: LLM Prompt Self-Replication
entries.rationale: Self-replicating prompts are text in the transcript and in files the agent writes.

entries.name: Discover LLM Hallucinations
entries.rationale: Adversary-side preparation on public or attacker-owned resources; nothing of it lands on the hosts, agents or accounts AgentDFIR examines.

entries.name: Discover AI Model Outputs
entries.rationale: Targets model training or inference internals (weights, datasets, inference APIs) that an endpoint and agent forensic tool does not collect.

entries.name: Gather RAG-Indexed Targets
entries.rationale: Adversary-side preparation on public or attacker-owned resources; nothing of it lands on the hosts, agents or accounts AgentDFIR examines.

entries.name: LLM Prompt Crafting
entries.rationale: Prompt crafting happens on adversary-controlled copies before delivery.

entries.name: Retrieval Content Crafting
entries.rationale: Crafted retrieval content is only visible when it is retrieved into the agent's context, where instruction content in tool results is flagged.

entries.name: LLM Trusted Output Components Manipulation
entries.rationale: Manipulated but plausible response components are in the transcript, but judging trustworthiness of model output is not a deterministic check.

entries.name: Citations
entries.rationale: Wrong or invented citations are in the transcript, but verifying them needs external lookups AgentDFIR does not make.

entries.name: LLM Prompt Obfuscation
entries.rationale: Invisible Unicode and other obfuscation in agent-facing content is checked byte by byte.

entries.name: Discover LLM System Information
entries.rationale: Discovery of system information shows up as extraction prompts or reads of agent configuration.

entries.name: Special Character Sets
entries.rationale: Probing for delimiters looks like ordinary text in a transcript; no deterministic signal separates it.

entries.name: System Instruction Keywords
entries.rationale: Probing for instruction keywords looks like ordinary text in a transcript; no deterministic signal separates it.

entries.name: System Prompt
entries.rationale: Requests for the system prompt are recorded in the transcript.

entries.name: RAG Poisoning
entries.rationale: The RAG store is not collected; poisoned entries are visible only when retrieved into a transcript.

entries.name: False RAG Entry Injection
entries.rationale: The RAG database is not collected; a false entry is visible only when retrieved into a transcript.

entries.name: Cyber Communication Channel
entries.rationale: Reverse shells, listeners, tunnels and connections the transcript does not explain are in commands and endpoint network telemetry.

entries.name: Impersonation
entries.rationale: Impersonation targets people through channels AgentDFIR does not examine.

entries.name: Masquerading
entries.rationale: Masquerading agent components show up as name collisions, look-alike packages and configuration symlinks in snapshots.

entries.name: Enterprise Resource Discovery
entries.rationale: Resource discovery runs as commands and connections (metadata endpoints, scans) the agent makes; legitimate inventory work looks the same.

entries.name: Corrupt AI Model
entries.rationale: A deliberately corrupted model file is not parsed by AgentDFIR; only a later unsafe load would be seen.

entries.name: LLM Response Rendering
entries.rationale: The rendered response is in the transcript, but whether the client fetched the embedded external reference is not recorded there.
entries.exception: No rule inspects assistant output for image or link references that carry conversation data to an external host; the transcript holds the response text but not whether the client rendered and fetched it, so a detection would claim more than the evidence shows. Revisit when a client-side fetch log is collected.

entries.name: Drive-by Compromise
entries.rationale: The compromised site is outside the examined systems; the content the agent fetched from it is in the transcript and checked for injected instructions.

entries.name: Stage Capabilities
entries.rationale: Adversary-side preparation on public or attacker-owned resources; nothing of it lands on the hosts, agents or accounts AgentDFIR examines.

entries.name: AI Agent Context Poisoning
entries.rationale: Poisoned context persists in memory and instruction files and in the transcript, which are compared against where each line came from.

entries.name: Memory
entries.rationale: Agent memory and instruction files are on disk and their provenance is reconstructed from the transcript.

entries.name: Thread
entries.rationale: Instructions injected into a thread are in that thread's transcript.

entries.name: Modify AI Agent Configuration
entries.rationale: Agent configuration is snapshotted and diffed, and writes to it are in commands and file events.

entries.name: RAG Credential Harvesting
entries.rationale: The RAG store is not collected; harvested credentials are observable when they appear in the conversation.

entries.name: Credentials from AI Agent Configuration
entries.rationale: Reads of agent credential stores are in commands and file events; inline secrets in MCP configuration are found in snapshots.

entries.name: Discover AI Agent Configuration
entries.rationale: Reads of agent configuration are commands in the transcript; an agent reading its own configuration is normal, so only enumeration is flagged.

entries.name: Embedded Knowledge
entries.rationale: Discovery of an agent's data sources is a read of its configuration, recorded as a command.

entries.name: Tool Definitions
entries.rationale: Enumerating tool definitions is a read of agent or MCP configuration, recorded as a command.

entries.name: Activation Triggers
entries.rationale: Activation triggers live in agent configuration whose reads are recorded as commands.

entries.name: Call Chains
entries.rationale: Call chains are read from agent configuration, recorded as commands.

entries.name: Data from AI Services
entries.rationale: Collection through AI services is recorded as tool calls, but retrieval is what those services are for; only a later exfiltration step is flagged.

entries.name: RAG Databases
entries.rationale: RAG retrievals are recorded as tool calls when a local agent makes them; volume alone is not a deterministic signal.

entries.name: AI Agent Tools
entries.rationale: Tool-based collection is recorded in transcripts and gateway logs, but it is indistinguishable from normal tool use until data leaves.

entries.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation
entries.rationale: Uploads, pushes and outbound tool calls made by the agent are in transcripts, gateway logs and endpoint telemetry, and are correlated with prior sensitive access.

entries.name: Gather Victim Identity Information
entries.rationale: Adversary-side preparation on public or attacker-owned resources; nothing of it lands on the hosts, agents or accounts AgentDFIR examines.

entries.name: Generate Deepfakes
entries.rationale: Deepfakes are generated on adversary infrastructure.

entries.name: Enterprise Environment Discovery
entries.rationale: Environment discovery runs as commands in transcripts and process telemetry; most of it is indistinguishable from routine work.

entries.name: OS Credential Dumping
entries.rationale: Credential dumping tools, hash-file reads and keychain access by agent processes are in commands and endpoint telemetry.

entries.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
entries.rationale: Use of alternate authentication material is mostly seen by the service it is presented to; the same credential reappearing across unrelated sessions is observable.

entries.name: Application Access Token
entries.rationale: Token use is logged by the service; on the host, token export and reuse across sessions are observable.

entries.name: Web Session Cookie
entries.rationale: Replaying a cookie happens at the web service; reading the browser cookie store on the host is observable.

entries.name: Manipulate User LLM Chat History
entries.rationale: Rewritten, truncated or replaced chat history is detected against the monitor journal and the transcript's own internal consistency.

entries.name: Prompt Infiltration via Public-Facing Application
entries.rationale: The public-facing application is outside the examined systems; the prompt is observable only once an agent ingests it.

entries.name: Delay Execution of LLM Instructions
entries.rationale: Deferred instructions sit in content or memory; standing instructions that order actions on every run are flagged, conditional triggers in general are not.

entries.name: Search Open Websites/Domains
entries.rationale: Adversary-side preparation on public or attacker-owned resources; nothing of it lands on the hosts, agents or accounts AgentDFIR examines.

entries.name: Code Repositories
entries.rationale: Adversary-side preparation on public or attacker-owned resources; nothing of it lands on the hosts, agents or accounts AgentDFIR examines.

entries.name: AI Service API
entries.rationale: Command-and-control through an AI service API blends into the agent's normal provider traffic; endpoint telemetry shows only the provider host.

entries.name: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion
entries.rationale: Sandbox checks are ordinary system queries; nothing deterministic separates them from routine environment inspection.

entries.name: AI Agent Tool Credential Harvesting
entries.rationale: Credentials returned by agent tools appear in the transcript or gateway log, and their onward transfer through another tool is chained.

entries.name: AI Agent Tool Data Poisoning
entries.rationale: Poisoned data reaches the agent as tool results, recorded in the transcript and gateway log and checked for instruction content.

entries.name: AI Agent Clickbait
entries.rationale: Computer-use actions are recorded as tool calls, but whether page content baited them is not a deterministic check.

entries.name: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation
entries.rationale: Destructive commands, cloud deletions and evidence-source deletions are in commands, endpoint telemetry and cloud audit logs.

entries.name: Generate Malicious Commands
entries.rationale: Generated commands are in the transcript and the rules judge each command, but not whether a model generated it for an adversary.

entries.name: Deploy AI Agent
entries.rationale: Agents launched headless with approvals off, nested agents and agents with no verified parent are visible in commands and lineage.

entries.name: Escape to Host
entries.rationale: Namespace entry, host mounts and privileged workloads are in endpoint telemetry and commands.

entries.name: Exploitation for Credential Access
entries.rationale: The exploit is not observable; honeytoken access catches the credential read whatever method produced it.

entries.name: Exploitation for Defense Evasion
entries.rationale: The exploited vulnerability is not observable; the resulting loss of telemetry and controls that the evidence contradicts is.

entries.name: AI Agent
entries.rationale: An agent abused as a command channel shows standing instructions that call out on every run and network activity its transcript does not explain.

entries.name: AI Supply Chain Rug Pull
entries.rationale: A rug pull is a change to an already-trusted component, visible as definition and capability drift between snapshots.

entries.name: AI Agent Tool Poisoning
entries.rationale: Tool definitions, skills and tool responses are captured and checked for instruction content and drift.

entries.name: Definition and Instructions
entries.rationale: Poisoned descriptions and skill instructions are in captured tool definitions and skill files.

entries.name: Implementation
entries.rationale: A poisoned implementation shows as observed effects (writes, deletes, network) that contradict the tool's declared schema or read-only annotation.

entries.name: Runtime Response
entries.rationale: Tool responses are recorded in the transcript and gateway log, checked for instruction content, and chained to the privileged action that follows.

entries.name: AI Supply Chain Reputation Inflation
entries.rationale: Reputation inflation happens on public registries and social platforms.

entries.name: Machine Compromise
entries.rationale: Umbrella for full compromise through AI components; the observable parts are mapped to its sub-techniques.

entries.name: Local AI Agent
entries.rationale: A local agent turned against its host leaves the full sequence (untrusted input, configuration change, execution) in its transcript and process lineage.

entries.name: AI Artifacts
entries.rationale: The malicious artifact is not scanned; loading it unsafely is observable.

entries.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
entries.rationale: Reads of browser cookie and credential stores by agent processes are in commands and file events.

entries.name: AI Service Web Interface
entries.rationale: Relaying commands through an AI service web interface looks like ordinary browsing to that service.

entries.name: Publish Poisoned AI Artifacts
entries.rationale: Publishing poisoned artifacts happens on public registries; their consumption is AML.T0010.

entries.name: Datasets
entries.rationale: Publishing poisoned datasets happens on public registries.

entries.name: Models
entries.rationale: Publishing poisoned models happens on public registries.

entries.name: AI Agent Tools
entries.rationale: Publishing a poisoned agent tool happens on public registries; installing it is AML.T0010.005.

entries.name: Autonomous Reconnaissance
entries.rationale: Autonomous reconnaissance is a run of discovery actions in one agent transcript; recon can also be legitimate.

entries.name: Autonomous Attack-Path Adaptation
entries.rationale: A refused or failed action followed by another attempt at the same target is in the transcript.

entries.name: Autonomous AI Agent Communication
entries.rationale: Messages between agents and subagents are recorded in their transcripts.

entries.name: Communication via Shared Artifacts
entries.rationale: Shared files written by one agent and read by another are in both transcripts and in file provenance.

entries.name: Direct Agent Communication
entries.rationale: Direct agent-to-agent messages are recorded in the transcripts of both sides.

entries.name: Exploit Automated Artifact Processing Pipeline
entries.rationale: The pipeline itself is not examined; repository content shaped to exploit it (shell syntax in ref names, risky lifecycle scripts) is.

entries.name: AI Artifact Repository
entries.rationale: Polling an artifact repository for tasking looks like ordinary package or model downloads.

entries.name: AI Agent Environment Reconstruction
entries.rationale: Reinstalling tools after a reset is recorded in the transcript, but it is indistinguishable from normal environment setup.

entries.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
entries.rationale: Exploit traffic against a remote service is network evidence AgentDFIR does not read; only its effects on examined hosts are visible.

entries.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
entries.rationale: Encoded payloads run through interpreters and obfuscated extension or agent-facing content are decoded and inspected.

entries.name: Autonomous Attack Orchestration
entries.rationale: Orchestration across hosts needs cross-case correlation; within a case, nested and runaway subagent spawning is observable.

entries.name: Create Account
entries.rationale: Local account creation and cloud identity creation are in commands, endpoint telemetry and cloud audit logs.

entries.name: Automated Collection
entries.rationale: Automated collection is the agent's normal mode of work; a session opened with an instruction to hunt for secrets is the observable signal.

entries.name: Data Staged
entries.rationale: Archiving and copying data into staging locations is in commands and file events.

entries.name: Compromise Infrastructure
entries.rationale: Compromised third-party infrastructure is outside the examined systems.

entries.name: Triggers in Multimodal Inputs
entries.rationale: A non-text input followed by a consequential action with no user text in between is visible in the transcript; the content of the image or audio is not analysed.

entries.name: AI Agent Response Biasing
entries.rationale: Biasing instructions planted in memory are flagged as context poisoning; biased answers themselves are not judged.

entries.name: Crafted AI Assistant Links
entries.rationale: Opening a prefilled assistant link is at most a browser-history URL; no rule separates crafted links from ordinary deep links.

entries.name: Misconfigured or Publicly Exposed AI Services
entries.rationale: Agent and MCP misconfiguration (plaintext transport, blanket trust, auto-approval) is read from configuration snapshots.

entries.name: Discover AI Agent Runtime Capabilities
entries.rationale: Asking an agent what it can do is ordinary text in the transcript; only explicit system-prompt extraction is flagged.

entries.name: AI Targeted Cloaking
entries.rationale: AgentDFIR sees what the agent received, never the different content served to humans or crawlers, so cloaking itself cannot be shown.
